# Reactivegas mutant ledger

<!-- Generated by `scripts/lean-mutants/run --write` from `lean/mutants/ledger.json`
     and `lean/mutants/catalogue.json`. `just lean-mutants` fails when this file
     differs from its rendering. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every authored theorem of the `Reactivegas` modules, with the shipped production
definition whose mutation makes it fail. A mutant changes one line of one
production definition. It **kills** a theorem when, under it, Lean reports an
error inside that theorem's own declaration **and** the mutated definition is
in the theorem's statement closure (the constants its type reaches through
definition bodies, never through proofs). CI re-runs every mutant on every
change and fails when a claim here is not what Lean reports.

- **KILLED** — the listed mutants each kill it.
- **HELPER** — its statement names no production definition (computed).
- **OPEN** — no admitted mutant killed it; the reason says why, and the
  attempted mutants are the ones whose target is in its statement closure.

## Limits

What a row here does not establish.

- A kill shows the theorem constrains that one edit of that definition; it says
  nothing about whether the definition is the right one for the product.
- Lean admits a theorem whose proof fails, so the error stays in that theorem's
  own declaration: a theorem whose proof only cites a killed theorem elaborates
  and is OPEN (`masked`). Its reason names the killed theorems it rests on.
- Modules that import a broken module are elaborated against it with its failed
  theorems admitted. An error such a cascade placed inside an owning theorem's
  declaration would be credited as a kill; nothing separates the two.
- Diagnostic positions and declaration ranges are compared as Lean reports them
  (line, codepoint column); multi-byte columns are not checked separately.
- Which arm of a guard a refusal-constructor mutant hits is the catalogue's
  label; the runner only checks that the mutated definition emits the
  constructor or is reached from a definition that does.
- The extent is the git-tracked Lean modules under `lean/`. CI also builds Lean
  tooling packages outside it (`scripts/lake-roots/`, the Lake-roots exe the
  mirror checker runs, and this runner's census and driver); a theorem authored
  there would get no row and nothing would object.
- Production is decided by the last component of a module's name (the rule is
  printed by `scripts/lean-mutants/run --census`). A further proof-only module
  whose name the rule does not list would be read as production: its
  definitions would be admitted as mutant targets and refusal emitters.
- The driver reproduces only the options Lake records in each module's setup;
  a run where Lake passes any other Lean argument fails instead.

## Excluded theorem constants

Rule: a theorem constant is EXCLUDED exactly when the elaborator, not a `theorem` command, produced it: the environment records no source declaration range of its own for it (equation, injectivity, sizeOf, auxiliary-proof and simp lemmas), or it is a structure projection (a `Prop` field of a structure); every other theorem constant is AUTHORED.
